title: Olaf Scholz delivers the Zeitenwende speech to the Bundestag
body:
On 27 February 2022, three days after Russia invaded Ukraine, German Chancellor Olaf Scholz addressed an emergency session of the Bundestag in Berlin. He described the invasion as a Zeitenwende, a "historic turning point". The speech marked a break with Germany's cautious post-war defence policy and with the long-standing opposition of Scholz's own Social Democratic Party to the NATO target of spending 2 percent of GDP on defence.

Scholz announced a one-off, off-budget special fund of 100 billion euros to modernise the Bundeswehr, and pledged that Germany would spend more than 2 percent of its GDP on defence. According to the account of the speech, Germany reached the 2 percent target in 2024. Nord Stream 2 was not part of the speech; Scholz had announced on 22 February that certification of the pipeline would be halted after Putin ordered troops into eastern Ukraine.

The Bundestag passed a motion condemning Russia with support from all parties except The Left and the Alternative for Germany. Opposition leader Friedrich Merz endorsed the defence agenda, and NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg praised the commitment. One poll found that 78 percent of Germans supported the policies. The Left criticised the higher military spending as an arms race. "Zeitenwende" was named German Word of the Year for 2022. Later assessments noted that the 100 billion euro fund was running low, and that a larger fund or budget expansion might be needed.
